title: Measure memory and IO pressure, ask again when a compute bottleneck outlives the founder's answer, name the heaviest measured workload, and verify a change before it is credited
problem: At b1950be2 (#196 head), greg/compute.py sampled load and disk only, so memory pressure, the real limit on a 4-8 GB Chromebook, could never be named a bottleneck. recommend() built request_id from the resource name alone ('req-compute-' + sha256_json({'resource': ...})), so after one answered cpu ask every later sustained cpu bottleneck produced the same id and recommend() returned None for good; this was reproduced on a real body with a signed DECISION (test key). The ask's first option was fixed text ('optimize the heaviest mission workload first') with nothing measuring which workload was heaviest. Nothing benchmarked the body and nothing checked whether a change helped. Directive section 48's chain (TELEMETRY, BOTTLENECK, QUANTIFY, TEST SOFTWARE OPTIMIZATION, ... BENCHMARK, VERIFY IMPROVEMENT) therefore stopped at BOTTLENECK, and only once per resource.
founder_intent_refs: INTENT-20261028-OPUS-MAXIMUS-REISSUE (directive sections 48 COMPUTE SCALING, 58 INFRASTRUCTURE SCALING CLOSURE, 60 GREG MAY ASK FOR RESOURCES and 71 TRUE OPUS MAXIMUS; recorded on #227)
INTENT-20261030-BUILD-BEFORE-DEVICE-RUN (build the whole directive first; the founder-device run comes after, as its acceptance; recorded on #227)

INTENT-2026-09-30-MASTER-BUILD-DIRECTIVE (section 60: every resource ask carries evidence, alternatives, costs, expected effect, uncertainty and authority requirements, with no manufactured urgency; implemented as the one path greg/asks.py)
INTENT-GREG-EMBODIED-2026-09-11 (justified compute growth on the owned body)
baseline: b1950be2: compute.sample() records cores, load1, load_ratio, memory_bytes and disk figures. bottleneck() fires on load_ratio >= 0.9 or free disk < 10% over the last 5 samples. recommend() keys the COMPUTE ask on the resource name only and returns None whenever a decision.requested row with that id exists, answered or not. The ask lists four fixed options (optimization, cloud burst, an additional node, do nothing) and says 'no ROI claim'. There is no step timing, no benchmark, no improvement check and no `greg compute` command. greg/body.py calls record_telemetry and recommend.

alternatives.name: Proposed (as built): pressure telemetry, an epoch-keyed re-ask, measured step timing, a stdlib benchmark and a contention-guarded verdict
alternatives.description: Only greg/compute.py (above enroll_node) and greg/cli.py change; greg/body.py's existing calls carry the new behaviour. sample() adds PSI 'some avg10/avg60' for cpu, memory and io, and MemTotal, MemAvailable and their ratio; an unreadable or negative field is None, never 0. Rules: memory (PSI avg60 >= 10% or MemAvailable/MemTotal < 10%), io (PSI avg60 >= 20%), precedence memory, io, cpu, disk, other held rules listed in also_sustained; a sample missing a field never counts. ask_state() reads COMPUTE asks through asks.open_requests and the mission book's counted answers: only a founder-signed answer or a withdrawal closes an ask. request_id carries an epoch (closed asks for that resource; epoch 0 keeps the old id). No ask while one is pending; a re-ask needs all 5 window samples after the close. step_times() reads the ledger's existing record times (latest mission.dispatching intent to first mission.action) and voids any step with a body-loop record between intent and outcome, recovered steps, capability-less outcomes and negative spans. quantify() names the capability with the largest share of timed step time in the window and labels the delay figure 'estimate (method: ...)'. benchmark() runs a fixed stdlib workload (seeded sha256 chain, scratch Journal/EvidenceLedger append-and-verify, one interpreter spawn) and measures per-replicate contention. verify_improvement() runs a one-sided rank-sum permutation test (exact up to 50,000 arrangements, alpha 0.05), a noise floor of the before run's IQR over its median, and returns VERIFIED only when contention did not ease in the after run's favour (tolerance 0.05). CLI: `greg compute status` (read-only via observe()), `benchmark --out FILE` (refuses the body home, never overwrites a non-benchmark file), `verify --before A --after B`.
advantages: A bottleneck that outlives the founder's answer is asked about again (live run: epoch-1 ask on the fifth sample after the signed answer), never while an ask is pending
Memory and IO pressure can be named (unit-tested); unreadable fields are None, never 0
The ask's optimization option names the measured heaviest workload (live run: fs.write, 100% of measured step time) and excludes founder approval waits and downtime

A before/after verdict that refused credit to host drift on this host: 0 of 9 same-code pairs VERIFIED with the guard (2 of 9 by statistics alone), the busy-loop pair INCONCLUSIVE, and a real code change VERIFIED 3 of 3
Stdlib only, no network, no prices fetched, no purchase; the CLI never writes the body ledger; greg/body.py unchanged
disadvantages: The contention guard is a proxy: drift that shows neither as descheduling nor as PSI stall time (frequency or thermal scaling, a cache-heavy neighbour) is not caught
On this busy shared host 6 of 9 same-code pairs were INCONCLUSIVE, so a noisy body may get few verdicts
After a signed reject GREG asks again one sustained window later (about 50 minutes at the default 30 s tick, telemetry every 20 ticks, 5 samples), indefinitely while the bottleneck holds
compute.benchmark and compute.improvement are not ledger records, and recommend() still runs uncontained in Body.run; both need greg/body.py
Section 48's economic model is not built: there is no founder-entered price, no payback figure, and the ask states 'unpriced: no ROI claim'
alternatives.revival_evidence: Retained as proposed; revisit on the first founder-device telemetry, on the founder's ruling on re-ask after a reject, or if a same-code series on founder hardware yields VERIFIED.

alternatives.name: Simplest viable: add the epoch and the pending block to request_id only
alternatives.description: Fix the defect that silenced a resource forever after one answered ask, and change nothing else.
advantages: Smallest change: one function in greg/compute.py
disadvantages: Memory pressure stays invisible, though it is the limit on the founder's 4-8 GB Chromebook
The ask still names no measured workload, so 'optimize first' has no target
No benchmark and no improvement check: section 48's BENCHMARK and VERIFY IMPROVEMENT steps stay absent
Leaves the unit's acceptance tests for memory, quantification, benchmark and verification unmet
alternatives.revival_evidence: If the founder rejects the telemetry, timing or benchmark parts, the epoch and pending block alone (ask_state and the request_id change) still stand as the defect fix.

alternatives.name: Strongest competing design: commodity monitoring and benchmarking (node_exporter/Prometheus alerting, pyperf or hyperfine, scipy.stats.mannwhitneyu)
alternatives.description: Collect pressure with a metrics agent and alert on it, benchmark with a dedicated harness, and test the difference with scipy, keeping only the COMPUTE ask in GREG.
advantages: Mature tools with calibrated warm-up, outlier and system-tuning handling (pyperf), and alert silencing and back-off (Alertmanager)
Dashboards and long retention come with them
disadvantages: None of pyperf, psutil, prometheus_client, hyperfine, node_exporter or prometheus is installed here, so nothing could be measured in this unit
An alert raised outside greg/asks.py is not a section 60 ask (evidence, alternatives, costs, expected effect, uncertainty, authority) and never reaches the founder's ask surfaces
scipy in greg/compute.py would make the body core depend on the optional cognition wheels (spec critique); the stdlib test matched it in the reviewer's check
A resident metrics daemon adds memory on the 4-8 GB body whose memory pressure it would measure
alternatives.revival_evidence: Preferred if a fleet of bodies (section 49) needs shared dashboards, or if the founder's device shows the stdlib benchmark too noisy to give verdicts; pyperf is the first candidate for the benchmark harness.

alternatives.name: Staged, reversible experiment: this branch as a draft child of #196
alternatives.description: The behaviour reaches the body only through its existing record_telemetry and recommend calls. An ask requests no spend and buys nothing; the CLI writes only the files it names. The founder sees the first real re-ask, named workload and verdicts on his own body before adoption; one revert removes the change.
advantages: No purchase, rental, installation, network call or new authority at any step
Old ledgers stay readable both ways: epoch 0 keeps the legacy id, and the old bottleneck() reads only load_ratio and disk_free_ratio
The trial exercises exactly what section 48 and section 71 describe, on founder hardware
disadvantages: Every result so far is from a shared Linux container with generated test keys
The re-ask cadence after a reject is live in the trial unless the founder rules on it first
alternatives.revival_evidence: This is how the proposed design is meant to be adopted; it is the review trigger for the decision below.

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: After one answered cpu ask GREG never asks about cpu again, however long the bottleneck lasts; memory pressure on a Chromebook is never named; 'optimize first' names no workload; and no growth decision can be checked by a benchmark. Section 48 stays stopped at BOTTLENECK, and section 71's 'I tested software optimization first' has nothing behind it.
advantages: No change to compute.py or cli.py
No new asks reach the founder
disadvantages: A reproduced defect silences a resource after its first answered ask
The body's real limit on founder hardware is unmeasured
No way to tell whether a change helped, or whether a speed-up was host drift

Now telemetry covers memory and io, QUANTIFY names the heaviest measured workload, the ask can be raised again, and BENCHMARK and VERIFY IMPROVEMENT exist as founder-run commands. Nothing is bought and nothing argues from the body's continuation.

pass_1.intended_outcome: The body measures the pressures that actually limit a small machine, keeps asking about a bottleneck that outlives an answer (one ask per resource at a time), names the measured heaviest workload so optimization is tried first, and lets the founder check whether a change measurably helped, with no purchase, network call or new authority.

advantages.statement: Memory and IO pressure are measured, and unreadable fields are None, never 0

pass_2.attack_summary: Re-attacked as deployed at 416a2e54 by two adversarial reviews done by separate agents of this same session (attack and fidelity), then verified again at 66f9d5ac. Targets: what step time actually measures, whether VERIFIED can be produced by the host alone, the CLI's write guard, crash paths in the body loop, test races, the mutant coverage claim, and whether the records claim more than the evidence shows.

new_weaknesses.statement: WU05-F1: a re-dispatch reused the deduplicated first intent, so the founder's approval wait and the body's downtime were booked as capability step time (4.266 s and 3.139 s reproduced on real bodies)
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Timing starts at the latest intent and is voided by any body-loop record between intent and outcome (LOOP_RECORDS); regression tests fail at 416a2e54; mutants for each record family

new_weaknesses.statement: WU05-F2 and F1-verify: VERIFIED for unchanged code when only host load changed; the start-of-run snapshots could point the wrong way
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Per-replicate contention (this process's off-CPU share during the chain, host PSI stall shares) and end conditions are recorded; VERIFIED needs contention measured during both runs and not eased in the after run's favour; every verdict carries its scope. Same-code series 0 of 9 VERIFIED, real code change 3 of 3

new_weaknesses.statement: WU05-F3: a home given as a literal '~/...' bypassed the --out guard, and the probe overwrote ledger.jsonl
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: The guard resolves the home through Layout(home).home, also checks samefile, and refuses to overwrite any file that is not an earlier benchmark result; a regression test and CLI mutants pin both

new_weaknesses.statement: WU05-F4: a None capability or a window of 0 s steps made recommend() raise TypeError, and recommend runs uncontained in Body.run

pass_2.final_design: As built at 66f9d5ac: PSI and MemAvailable telemetry with None for unreadable fields; memory, io, cpu and disk rules with declared precedence; ask state read through asks.open_requests with an epoch in request_id, no ask while pending and a re-ask only after a full window measured after the close; step timing from the latest intent, voided by any body-loop record before the outcome; the heaviest workload named in the ask and the delay labelled an estimate; a stdlib benchmark with per-replicate contention; a one-sided permutation verdict that also requires contention not to have eased in the after run's favour and states its scope; a read-only `greg compute status`, a guarded `benchmark --out`, and `verify`. 48 tests and 51 caught mutants.

residual_risks.mitigation: Verdicts carry their scope; the round-1 drift VERIFIED is kept as a labelled negative; ABAB interleaving is recorded as dissent
residual_risks.review_trigger: A same-code VERIFIED on founder hardware

residual_risks.mitigation: Recorded here for the integrator; Canonical CI runs on Linux runners

dissent.handling: Recorded with thresholds; neither entry blocks a draft. The first blocks adoption until the founder rules on re-ask after a reject; the second blocks any growth decision that rests on a single VERIFIED from a noisy host.

entries.position: Do not let GREG re-ask after a signed reject until the founder chooses a back-off or a signed 'stop asking about this resource' control.
entries.rationale: Section 60 forbids manufactured urgency. Before this unit a rejected compute ask was never repeated; now it is repeated about every 50 minutes while the bottleneck holds.
entries.evidence_threshold: A founder ruling, or a re-ask rule that after a reject requires a measured change in the bottleneck metrics

entries.position: Before a growth decision rests on VERIFIED, interleave before and after replicates (ABAB) in one invocation, or re-run the baseline (A-B-A), instead of relying on the contention proxy alone.
entries.rationale: The proxy cannot see frequency or thermal scaling or cache contention, and 2 of 2 false positives caught is not a false-positive rate.
entries.evidence_threshold: A same-code series on founder hardware with any VERIFIED, or a pre-registered false-positive measurement above alpha
entries.review_trigger: The first founder use of `greg compute verify` for a growth decision

authority_impact.approver: Alfonso Lopez (adoption, any merge, the re-ask cadence after a reject, and the pressure thresholds); #196 integrator for intake

migration_plan: None required. The new telemetry fields are additive; older samples without them never count as memory or io pressure, because a missing field never counts. Epoch 0 keeps the legacy request_id, so a ledger that already holds a COMPUTE ask is not asked twice. Benchmark results are plain JSON files outside the body home.

steps: Revert this branch's commits, or decline intake into #196

No data migration: the old bottleneck() reads only load_ratio and disk_free_ratio, so extra telemetry fields are ignored; an epoch-1 ask already on a ledger stays as a recorded ask, and the old recommend() finds its own epoch-0 id present and asks nothing new
Benchmark files written by the CLI can be left or deleted; nothing in the body reads them

kill_criteria: A COMPUTE ask raised while another ask for the same resource is pending, or a re-ask without a full SUSTAINED_SAMPLES window measured after the close
An unreadable telemetry field recorded as 0, or a missing field counted as pressure
`greg compute` writing to the body home or ledger, or compute.py making a network call, purchase, rental or installation
A same-code VERIFIED on founder hardware that the contention guard does not explain, repeated in a pre-registered series
The founder rules that re-asking after a reject is pressure and no back-off is built: then regress the re-ask to answers other than reject
decision_owner: Alfonso Lopez decides adoption, the re-ask cadence after a reject (back-off or a signed stop-asking control) and the pressure thresholds; the #196 integrator decides intake and wires the mutant gate into canonical-ci.yml; session_01Kucyfm6YBHMTjaiC1M9hqD owns the reversible draft. Three roles recommend RETAIN, the Adversarial Reviewer recommends EXPERIMENT, and the Evidence and Welfare Guardian asks for the founder's decision.
